hypotheses.reasoning: notification-svc (v4.16.1) runs out of heap while growing an unbounded messageCache: 'heap exhausted while growing messageCache (requested 64MB, max 1536MB)' at #3834, followed by the OOM-killer restarting the process (#3837). The pod is then OOMKilled again at #4212 and #4629 (restarts=3), and each restart re-warms the cache and dies again. While the process is down or restarting, api-gateway's POST /v1/notify calls fail with 502 'upstream notification-svc connection reset (no healthy upstream)' (#3930, #4154, and later), which is the paged symptom. Heap was steady at 30-47% through 14:21 (DEBUG GC lines), so growth was steady and cumulative, not a sudden spike. The template-svc circuit-breaker trip at #1883 was brief and template-svc recovered immediately, so it is not the origin. Red herrings: the report-cron pandas ModuleNotFoundError (#2000), the account-svc status_v2 column errors (#3587, #3788), and the legacy-inventory timeouts in status-poller are real faults but do not touch the notify path. The 429 throttle on k-7148 (#3962) is client-side rate limiting, not the 502 source.

A notif-worker v1.2.6 rollout appears at #3350, but it is a worker, not the notify request path, and the OOM is in notification-svc. Not supported as the origin unless the notification-svc v4.16.1 release also changed the cache policy, which the logs do not show.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately mitigate by scaling notification-svc or raising the memory limit so restarts stop, and by capping messageCache size or enabling eviction (roll back to the prior cache configuration if v4.16.1 changed it). Review the /tmp/heap.hprof heap dump to confirm what is retained. Separately, fix the report-cron image missing pandas, the account-svc status_v2 column mismatch on accounts-db, and the deprecated legacy-inventory healthcheck in status-poller.
